nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ (with $t_0 = a$) satisfies $t_j = 0$ for some $j \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Pierce trajectories vanish at a positive step

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory: $t_0 = a$, and $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ if $t_j \ne 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$. Then $t_i = 0$ for some $i \le a + 1$.
nodes.title: A bound on when a Pierce trajectory vanishes

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le P(n)$, where $P(n) = \max_{1 \le b \le n} \ell(n, b)$ is the maximal Pierce length.
nodes.title: Each Pierce length is at most the maximal Pierce length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $a$ and $j$ with $j \ge 1$, if the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_j = 0$, then the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le j$.
nodes.title: The Pierce length is at most any positive vanishing step

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Pierce length is positive

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory, with $t_0 = a$, $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ if $t_j \ne 0$ and $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$. The Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ is the least $j \ge 1$ with $t_j = 0$; such a $j$ always exists.
nodes.title: Pierce length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $L$ be natural numbers. If the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le L$ for every $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, then the maximal Pierce length $P(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} \ell(n, a)$ (which is $0$ when $n = 0$) satisfies $P(n) \le L$.
nodes.title: A uniform bound on Pierce lengths bounds the maximal Pierce length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the maximal Pierce length $P(n)$ is the maximum of the Pierce lengths $\ell(n, a)$ over $1 \le a \le n$, with $P(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Maximal Pierce length

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_{\ell(n, a)} = 0$, where $\ell(n, a)$ is the Pierce length.
nodes.title: The Pierce trajectory vanishes at the Pierce length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $a$ and $j$ with $1 \le j < \ell(n, a)$, where $\ell(n, a)$ is the Pierce length, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_j \ne 0$.
nodes.title: The Pierce trajectory is nonzero before the Pierce length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t \ne 0$. Then the Pierce remainder trajectory of $t$ with respect to $n$ is, at step $1$, equal to $n \bmod t$, the remainder of $n$ modulo $t$.
nodes.title: First step of the Pierce trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then $t_{j+1} = 0$.
nodes.title: Step of the Pierce trajectory at a zero term

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j \ne 0$, then $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$, the remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$.
nodes.title: Step of the Pierce trajectory at a nonzero term

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ has value $a$ at step $0$.
nodes.title: Initial term of the Pierce trajectory

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is the sequence $t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ of natural numbers with $t_0 = a$ and, for every $j \ge 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$, while if $t_j \ne 0$ then $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ is the remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$. Once the trajectory reaches $0$ it stays there.
nodes.title: Pierce remainder trajectory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
